title: HRA Rules Revised: Bigger Tax Benefits for Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad
description: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has expanded the list of cities considered "metro" for House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption purposes. Bengaluru, Hyde.

faq.q: Is HRA exemption available under the New Tax Regime?
faq.a: No, HRA exemption is not available under the New Tax Regime. It is an exemption exclusively offered under the Old Tax Regime.

faq.q: Which cities are now considered metro for HRA purposes?
faq.a: From Financial Year 2026-27, eight cities are classified as metro for HRA exemption: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, and Ahmedabad.

faq.q: When do these new HRA rules become effective?
faq.a: The expanded metro city list for HRA exemption is effective from Financial Year 2026-27, meaning it applies to income earned from April 1, 2026, onwards.

faq.q: Do I need my landlord's PAN for HRA claims?
faq.a: Yes, if your annual rent paid exceeds ₹1 lakh, it is mandatory to provide your landlord's PAN. If they don't have one, you need a declaration from them.

faq.q: Can I claim HRA if I pay rent to my parents?
faq.a: Yes, you can claim HRA if you pay rent to your parents, provided the transaction is genuine and properly documented with a rent agreement and receipts. From April 1, 2026, you may also need to disclose the relationship.

faq.q: What does "salary" mean for HRA calculation?
faq.a: For HRA calculation, "salary" refers to the sum of your Basic Salary, Dearness Allowance (if it forms part of your retirement benefits), and any commission received as a percentage of turnover.
